basics.name: Alfredo Castañeda Sierra
basics.headline: Senior Software Engineer leading front-end teams. Looking for Engineering Manager or Tech Lead roles.

about: I'm a front-end engineer with more than ten years of experience building web products in Mexico City and Berlin, currently at Netflix. For the last few years I've been leading a team of five engineers in practice, and that has become the part of the job I enjoy most: seeing people grow.

Everyone is driven by something different. I like finding what that is and helping people build on it: connecting them with other teams, building trust and confidence, and making sure they see the value of their work. Some of the engineers I work with want to go deeper technically than I do, and I want to help them get there. That's why I'm looking for an Engineering Manager or Tech Lead role.

work.summary: Studio talent data: records of the people who work on Netflix productions, such as actors, directors, producers and animators.
highlights: Tech lead in practice for a team of 5 engineers: the bridge between product, design and engineering. I prioritize and assign work, and help review technical decisions.
Mentor 4–5 engineers, through a formal mentorship program and informally, supporting them through promotions and turnarounds.

Owned the architecture, much of the implementation and the launch communication for the Studio Talent Data components: a shared library for searching, displaying and creating talent records, used in 6+ apps across the organization.

Built, together with the data management team, tools to find and merge duplicate people: clusters of similar records, a graph of connections with confidence scores, and tables comparing their titles and roles. Together we reduced duplicate records by 75% in one year.

Replaced search and creation flows repeated across 6 apps with shared micro front-end modules (Webpack Module Federation). This removed 2k+ lines of code, kept every app on the same data rules and UX, and reduced bad data entering the talent services.

work.summary: Inventory tools for suppliers and warehouses.
highlights: Owned the front end on a full-stack team of 8–10 engineers, and also contributed to PHP and Java services.

Launched the new inventory management tool to ~100–150 suppliers that didn't have automated integrations, or were still building trust with Wayfair. Fewer orders failed because of missing inventory, so Wayfair's trust in those suppliers grew.
Moved tools built with custom JS frameworks and jQuery to React, removed duplicated code, and redesigned data-heavy tables, using Web Workers to keep large updates fast.

work.summary: Website builder: first used by in-house designers, then launched as Sitejet so small businesses could build their own sites from those templates.
highlights: Led and implemented the migration of the main CMS from jQuery to React and Vue, including choosing the new technologies. About 50% was migrated when I left.
Built a project management tool for businesses and agencies to track site progress, launches and billing, and to buy and manage domains, all connected to the design CMS.
Helped build DataLift 360, the dashboard and platform where advertisers managed budgets and campaigns.
Built visualizations of campaign performance that helped customers manage their budgets better.

work.position: Sr. Front End / Web UI Developer
highlights: Built a single workspace for Grey Advertising to track one client's campaigns across different locations: an AngularJS / Angular Material SPA with a Node.js bridge to the Box API (JWT auth).
Worked with several Autodesk teams to deliver a new version of their application.
Mentored developers on the team to reach sprint and project goals.
Turned client designs into websites and Drupal-based content management systems, from mockup to launch.
Built back-end components connecting sites to external web services.

languages.level: Intermediate (reading and writing stronger than speaking)
